statement: A graph (simple undirected graph) is a pair G = (V, E), where V is a set whose elements are called vertices, and E is a set of unordered pairs {v_1, v_2} of vertices, whose elements are called edges.

symbols.meaning: set of edges (links or lines), where each element is an unordered pair of vertices
order of the graph, defined as the number of vertices |V|
size of the graph, defined as the number of edges |E|
adjacency matrix of the graph, where A_ij specifies the number of connections from vertex i to vertex j

properties.property: The edges of a graph define a symmetric adjacency relation on the vertices, where vertices u and v are adjacent if {u, v} is an edge.
properties.why: Edges are unordered pairs of vertices

properties.property: In a simple graph of order n, the maximum degree of each vertex is n - 1, and the maximum number of edges is n(n - 1)/2.
properties.why: No loops or multiple edges are permitted, bounding connections to distinct other vertices

properties.property: An undirected graph is fully determined by a symmetric adjacency matrix A where A_ij = A_ji (and A_ii = 0 for simple graphs).
properties.why: Adjacency is symmetric for undirected edges and simple graphs contain no self-loops

properties.property: The degree or valency of a vertex is the number of edges incident to it.
properties.why: It counts the edges that join the vertex to another vertex

assumptions.assumption: The vertex set V is finite (which implies that the edge set E is also finite).
assumptions.breaks_when: Infinite graphs are considered, which are viewed as special binary relations and where finite graph theorems may fail or require different proofs.

assumptions.assumption: Edges are unordered pairs of distinct vertices (simple graph with no loops and no multiple edges).
assumptions.breaks_when: Multigraphs (multiple edges sharing the same endpoints) or graphs with loops (edges joining a vertex to itself) are permitted.
Directed graphs (edges are ordered pairs of vertices) or mixed graphs are used.

failure_modes.cause: The vertex set is empty, rendering terms requiring vertices or positive order undefined or degenerate.
Standard graph theory defines size as |E|, whereas algorithmic complexity contexts define size as |V| + |E| to avoid non-empty graphs having size 0.

failure_modes.signature: Vertex degree is 0, and no path exists connecting certain pairs of vertices.
failure_modes.cause: A vertex in V does not belong to any edge in E.
